_causes.reauthor-untracked: The two license re-authoring steps (manifest 28 reauthor_kanji_apply.py, 29 reauthor_vocab_apply.py) replace the verbatim KANJIDIC2 / JMdict text with our own authored glosses. Their inputs live under research/derived/reauthor/, which .gitignore excludes, so a rebuild ships the upstream dictionary wording and the committed export ships the authored wording: senses, their pos/misc/field/register and both locales of every gloss differ. Run against a checkout that has those trees, both steps apply cleanly (2,131 kanji, 2,678 vocab).
_causes.tr-untracked: The whole translation pipeline is off: tr_load.py (four tasks), tr_form_meanings.py, the thirteen gt_audit_apply.py field-classes, descaffold_apply.py and apply_full_audit.py all read research/derived/tr/, which .gitignore excludes. That is where the `en` locale comes from and where the audited pt-BR wording was corrected, so the rebuild has neither. Nine repair steps downstream (manifest 96-108) then find their anchors missing and refuse every row, which removes their corrections too. Restoring the trees turns 22 failing steps into 8.
_causes.n3-ptbr-lost: The N3 pt-BR workflow output (manifest 25-27) was never written to disk under a stable name and cannot be recovered from git, so the N3 kanji/vocab/grammar pt-BR that pass loaded is absent.
_causes.families-order: build_families_full.py is scoped to 'every N5/N4 item' (its own docstring) but sits after the N3 and N2/N1 bank ingests in the order a rebuild must run them, so it families the whole registry: 546 families / 12,759 members against the committed 396 / 2,572. The committed export was built before those levels existed. Fixing this means either scoping the script by level or moving it, and both change what the course sees — W01 follow-up, not a silent re-run.
_causes.readings-accumulated: db/corpus.sqlite holds 286 reading rows, the union of every historical run of build_readings.py against a lesson set that kept changing. One replay of today's script over today's lessons builds 130. This is the clearest single example of the general problem: the database is an accumulation, the manifest is one ordered pass.
_causes.course-identity: Lesson files differ mostly in cumulative_known_set / unlocks / srs card ids: the same headword resolves to a different vocab id because the sense set it is resolved against comes from reauthor_vocab_apply.py, which a clean clone cannot run. The prose differences on top of that are the nine refused repair steps and the missing en locale.
_causes.rollup: An INDEX / manifest / outline file: it summarises the records above, so it differs whenever any of them does.
_causes.not-committed: The rebuild produces this file and the repo does not have it. Not necessarily a defect — the renumbered topic directories and the exam-kanji lessons land here — but each one needs a look before it is called expected.
